box: The invariant under test is NOT 'the chip row's getBoundingClientRect().top does not move between tap-0 and tap-1' — src/games/daily-fortune.ts renderResult() (:221-243) calls stage.replaceChildren() on tap-0, so the chip row does not exist after it; a delta against a destroyed node measures absence, not stability, and would read as a pass while proving nothing (coordinator correction, superseding the original brief). The revised invariant: after tap-0, a second tap at the SAME screen coordinate as tap-0's chip cannot land on a different person, and cannot trigger navigation the group did not ask for.
method: Two independent evidence legs, per the coordinator's correction. Leg 1 (source-level, 0 browser runs): reveal() at src/games/daily-fortune.ts:245-251 runs synchronously from the chip's click handler (on(chip,'click',()=>reveal(name)) at :214) straight into renderResult()'s stage.replaceChildren() — no setTimeout, no requestAnimationFrame, no await anywhere on that path. Zero async hops means the love-match double-tap failure class (a re-render between tap-0 and tap-1 reflows the row so tap-1 lands on a different target) is structurally impossible here: there is no window in which a second tap could even be registered against the pre-tap DOM, because the DOM the group is looking at has already been replaced by the time the click handler returns. Leg 2 (browser, scripts/driver.mjs, real headless Chrome --headless --disable-gpu --no-sandbox --remote-debugging-port=9222, real build npm run build + npx serve dist/ -l 4321, script /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-waris-c-claude-free-game/90585d81-312d-4b66-bf93-10f22e00c6bd/scratchpad/daily-fortune-tap1-target.mjs, not committed -- scratchpad only, reproducible from this method description): navigated to /game/daily-fortune/ FIRST, then session.setWidth(320,900), wiped storage on-origin and reloaded, re-verified innerWidth===320 and localStorage/sessionStorage both empty (browser-verification.md traps 1 and 4). Added two roster names via a real native-setter 'input' event on #roster-add-name + a real .click() on #roster-add-btn, ticked both roster checkboxes, clicked #start-round, waited 600ms for the async mount (src/pages/game/[id].astro awaits a dynamic import before game.mount()). Located the first player's chip button, read its getBoundingClientRect() center (x,y) — tap-0's screen coordinate — and confirmed document.elementFromPoint(x,y) resolves to that exact chip BEFORE tapping (sanity check on the coordinate itself). Then performed a real .click() on that chip with NO artificial wait inserted (deliberately: the path is fully synchronous per leg 1, and inserting a wait would not test the real transition), and immediately read document.elementFromPoint(x,y) again at the SAME coordinate — now on the result screen — reporting its tag, a text snippet, whether it is an <a>, and whether any ancestor up to the stage is an <a> with an href (the only residual risk the coordinator named: an accidental hub-link hit, an annoyance rather than data loss since the fortune is deterministic per day). Screenshots taken before/after in scratchpad (not committed, per house convention). Positive control: kept from the original run against love-match at 05b103a (git worktree, port 4322) — see 'positiveControl' below — but it calibrates the APPARATUS (proves scripts/driver.mjs's evaluate()/getBoundingClientRect() mechanics work end to end against a real pre-fix build) and explicitly does NOT calibrate the daily-fortune claim above: different DOM (a persistent chip row with a header-length mechanism vs. a chip row destroyed on tap-0), different transition (header text swap in place vs. full stage.replaceChildren()). The coordinator independently confirmed on real iOS WebKit that a flex row's own container top is insensitive to chips being removed from inside it (delta stayed 0.00 even with a genuine reflow), which is consistent with this run's own 0px delta on the love-match positive control -- the container-top metric was never a proxy for the double-tap class either; it only ever measured the header-length-push sub-mechanism.

verdict: CORRECTED BY ADVERSARIAL RE-RUN BEFORE COMMIT. Original verdict ("PROVEN ... never on a different person or a navigating element") was falsified: it was measured with a 2-name roster only. An independent re-run with an 8-name roster, same apparatus (scripts/driver.mjs, real headless Chrome, real dist/, 320px, innerWidth===320 confirmed), found two CONFIRMED counter-examples -- recorded below in `counterExamples`. The tap-1-target claim HOLDS for the 2-name roster measured in leg 2 below (kept, unmodified) and FAILS at larger rosters: the double-tap-lands-elsewhere class IS reachable in daily-fortune, via the post-tap DOM placing interactive and navigating elements at coordinates the pre-tap DOM abandoned. Leg 1's reasoning (replaceChildren() destroys the pre-tap chip row synchronously, with no async hop for a second tap to land on the OLD DOM) still stands as far as it goes -- it was never wrong about the pre-tap DOM being destroyed. What it missed: a second tap can still hit something on the NEW (post-tap) DOM that happens to sit at the same screen coordinate, and at larger rosters that something can be a chip for a different person or the site-hub link.

containerTopObservableFailureNote: Run against known-buggy commit 05b103a (the parent of the love-match double-tap fix), the container-top delta returned 0px -- a 0 on a known-bad input does not calibrate the apparatus, it disqualifies the container-top observable as a detector for this bug class. This capture's claim does not rest on that observable: leg 2 above used document.elementFromPoint at daily-fortune's abandoned tap-0 coordinate, not chipRowTop. The elementFromPoint detector WAS independently calibrated on a known-bad case, on real iOS WebKit at 320px, where it reported the tracked chip moving y 171.0 -> 118.0 and a different person's chip occupying the original coordinate (recorded in scratchpad/IOS-WEBKIT-PLAYBOOK.md; reusable probe at scratchpad/webkit-probe/{frame,inner}.html). The container-top observable should not be reused for chip-row questions: a flex row's own top is insensitive to chips reflowing inside it.
calibrationDeltaVarianceNote: The 'y 171.0 -> 118.0' (delta 53) cited above and docs/verification/evidence/34/14-ios-webkit-first-real-engine.json's q1_positiveControl_frameHtml re-run of the SAME probe ('69.0 -> 12.0', delta 57) do not reconcile numerically -- two committed captures citing conflicting pixel deltas for one probe. Not a constant offset (53 vs 57 differ by 4, not by a fixed frame-origin shift), and this was not re-run to find out why. Do not cite either number as a precise figure. What DID reproduce in both runs, and is what this capture's claims rest on: the tracked chip moved, and a different person's chip ended up occupying the coordinate the tracked chip abandoned -- the qualitative finding, not the exact pixels.

positiveControl.interpretation: 0px delta even at the pre-fix commit. Consistent with the coordinator's independent real-iOS-WebKit finding that a flex row's own container top is insensitive to chips changing inside it -- this metric was never a valid detector for the double-tap reflow class (which shifts individual chip positions, not the row container's top), only for the separate header-length-push sub-mechanism, and at 24 Thai characters the pre-fix header still fit on one line at 320px so that sub-mechanism did not fire either. Retained here as an honest negative result, not as proof the apparatus can detect a non-zero delta -- see the coordinator's correction for why this run cannot serve that role for the tap-1-target claim above.
